articles.title: Championship roundup: Priske’s double gives Birmingham victory over Lincoln
articles.summary: Norwich battle back from two down against Watford. Preston remain rock bottom after defeat at Stoke. August Priske scored twice as Birmingham bounced back from defeat at Cardiff to beat Lincoln 3-1 at Sincil Bank and move – at least temporarily – into second.
body: Birmingham went ahead in the 16th minute with a goal owing to some fortune as a pass was inadvertently directed towards his own goal by Yunus Konak, straight to Priske on the edge of the area and he swivelled and fired a low shot into the bottom corner.

Ethan Laird could have seen red after half an hour after attempting to bring down a clearance but booting Ben House in the face as the Lincoln forward attempted to seize possession and nip in towards goal. Lewis Smith produced only a yellow card.
Huddersfield seized the bragging rights in the West Yorkshire derby as the leaders secured an emphatic 3-0 win at Bradford, who had their captain, Antoni Sarcevic, sent off.

An overhead kick from Joe Low gave the visitors an early lead before two goals in six minutes at the start of the second half from Derensili Sanches Fernandes and Joe Taylor made sure of the win. Bradford went down to 10 men in the 69th minute when Sarcevic was given a second booking for pulling back Ilias Bronkhorst.

articles.title: Man Utd make it 10 games unbeaten in goalless draw at Everton
articles.summary: Manchester United extended their unbeaten run to 10 matches in all competitions but they failed to fire in a 0-0 Women's Super League draw at Everton.
body: United went close to a late winner when Elisabeth Terland raced on to Jess Park's throughball, but the Norway striker was denied by Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan's save.
Everton's best chances fell to Ornella Vignola, but she twice fired shots straight at United goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce.
It was a game that lacked in quality, with both sides' defences comfortably dealing with the few chances created.

articles.title: Manchester United miss chance to close on WSL top three in drab draw at Everton
articles.summary: A group of well-choreographed, fancy-dress-wearing school-age dancers fully embraced the Halloween spirit as they boogied to one of Michael Jackson’s greatest hits at half-time. Alas, the football match itself was no thriller.
body: For Manchester United, the only scary thing about this game was how few times they tested Courtney Brosnan in Everton’s goal in the first 75 minutes as the visitors demonstrated a lack of creativity.

Brosnan did well to save from Elisabeth Terland’s strike, as United grew into the game late on and began to apply some pressure, but this was a fixture worthy of finishing goalless, or – as Sky Sports put it – ghoul-less.
Terland has scored five Women’s Super League goals against Everton, but Brosnan was equal to her close-range shot after Jess Park’s through ball.

“It was not a good performance but we aren’t always going to perform amazing or good,” said the Manchester United head coach, Eva Olid. “But it’s [about] always finding a way to win and today we didn’t.

articles.title: Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red card
articles.summary: Get ready for another week of agonising over the sorry state of Manchester United. The legends of old will rage, clips of a fuming Gary Neville will fly around social media, the airwaves will reverberate with complaints from angry supporters and by the time United play again there is every chance a…
body: There were echoes of Erik ten Hag’s final game in charge as the walls closed in on Michael Carrick at Stamford Bridge. United missed chances at 0-0, just as they did when Ten Hag lost to West Ham a day before his sacking two years ago, and Chelsea exacted punishment after initially delivering a performance so bad it had you worrying for the nascent Xabi Alonso project.

Chelsea were appalling during the first half, so it was just as well their opponents were in a giving mood. United had opportunities to make their decision to give Carrick a stay of execution look like a wise move rather than the consequence of executive-level confusion, but the finishing was awful and the defending was worse. Morgan Rogers cantered past five players to make it 1-0 and a seventh defeat in 13 games was confirmed when Lisandro Martínez’s faux hard man act saw him sent off after conceding the penalty that allowed Cole Palmer to seal Chelsea’s rise into fourth place.

articles.title: Pogacar 'happy to be alive' after 'scary' crash
articles.summary: Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar says he is "just happy to be alive", two months after suffering three fractured vertebrae in a crash.
body: The 28-year-old Slovenian was ruled out for the season after crashing during the Vuelta a Espana in August.
Pogacar required surgery on a broken collarbone and was initially diagnosed with a fracture in his neck, but further scans in his home country revealed more injuries.
"I knew I had a C7 fracture, but then we saw I had two more broken vertebrae, the T1 and T2," Pogacar told The Athletic, external.

"At that moment, I was happy I didn't do the European Championships, which had been my initial goal. When I saw I had three broken vertebrae? I'm just happy to be alive actually, or just to be standing."

articles.title: Kane beat Mbappe to Ballon d'Or by just 28 points
articles.summary: Voting figures show Harry Kane beat second-placed Kylian Mbappe to the men's Ballon d'Or by one of the tightest winning margins in the award's history.
body: Organisers released voting numbers on Saturday, showing that England captain Kane was awarded 1,055 points, compared with 1,027 for Real Madrid's France forward Mbappe.

Bayern Munich striker Kane became the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, while France talisman Mbappe also claimed his best finish, ending up well clear of Spain forward Lamine Yamal, who was third with 881 points.

It was the smallest winning margin since Argentina great Lionel Messi beat Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk by seven points in 2019, while the men's Ballon d'Or has twice been decided by a single point.

That happened when England World Cup winner Bobby Charlton, who was later knighted, beat Portugal star Eusebio by the smallest possible margin in 1966, and Germany defender Matthias Sammer repeated the tight one-point victory when he edged out Brazil striker Ronaldo in 1996.

articles.title: ‘Un-Australian’ - Warner tears into former side after South Africa seal series victory
articles.summary: David Warner branded Australia’s performance “un-Australian” and “disgraceful” after they were bowled out for just 111 to suffer defeat in the deciding Test in Cape Town.
body: South Africa won by 176 runs, took the series 2-1 and knocked Australia off the top of the Test rankings.
Warner, who opened for Australia until retiring from Test cricket in 2024, did not hold back on Fox Sports.

"It is terrible. It is un-Australian. There is no fight whatsoever. It is disgraceful," Warner said. "The batters have let the bowlers down all series. Matt Renshaw showed fight in that first Test, but I think the batters have been utterly disgraceful."
Renshaw was caught down the leg side off Kagiso Rabada in the opening over, a dismissal that drew little sympathy from Warner.

articles.title: South Africa win decider over Aussies to take series and go top of Test rankings
articles.summary: South Africa thumped Australia by 176 runs at Newlands as the hosts' bowling attack produced fireworks to clinch a 2-1 victory in the three-match series between the countries and propel the Proteas to the top of the ICC Men's Test Team Rankings.
body: This wasn't a chase that drifted away; it was snatched from Australia early on. Kagiso Rabada ripped through it in the first over and spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 to destroy any hopes of a comeback.
Set a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the Test world rankings for the first time since January 2016.

Matt Renshaw was caught by Ryan Rickelton down the leg side for a golden duck and Marnus Labuschagne was lbw for four. Travis Head followed for 14, caught by Marco Jansen at gully, as Rabada (3-39) took his 350th Test wicket.
That landmark made Rabada the quickest bowler to 350 Test wickets by balls bowled. He got there in 13,808 deliveries, ahead of compatriot Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan's ‌Waqar Younis (14,905).

articles.title: Henry impressed with the impact Arsenal stars are making off the bench
articles.summary: Arsenal have benefited from the contributions of their substitutes this season, with players coming off the bench regularly making a difference in matches. The Gunners will hope that trend continues as some of their starting players have found it difficult to break down opponents.
body: Every member of the squad has a role to play, and Mikel Arteta needs his players to perform whenever they are called upon. A team cannot rely on only a handful of individuals to deliver consistently, particularly over a long campaign involving several competitions.

There will inevitably be matches when only a few players perform well, while substitutes sometimes struggle to influence proceedings. Arsenal, however, have enjoyed a different experience this season. Their players coming off the bench have contributed goals and helped change the direction of games.

The club increasingly sees its squad depth as an important way to unlock opponents in the second half. That contribution could become even more significant as the fixtures get tougher and the Gunners face teams capable of making life difficult for their starting line up.
Thierry Henry has been encouraged by the impact of Arsenal’s bench, particularly because the team have continued to win matches even when their starters have not been at their best.

articles.title: What Chelsea Did Right vs Manchester United
articles.summary: In the early hours of Saturday morning Stamford Bridge played host to two of the Premier League’s biggest names. Michael Carrick saw the pressure around him ramp up as his Manchester United side’s wasteful first half turned into a dismal 2-0 defeat that could have easily been more.
body: With Jordan Henderson out and the Red Devils pressing hard from the front, the midfield set up in a different combination than we have seen recently. When it is Moises Caicedo with Henderson, they’re trusted to be further apart and drift as needed which in some games has created big gaps that the players couldn’t get by.

This time around, Alonso had Caicedo and Romeo Lavia very close together. This is a holdover from his Bayer Leverkusen team where the two midfielders would remain close together and keep possession. It worked to a treat here as Lavia had an absolute masterclass, allowing the attackers and wide defenders to spread the back line and create openings.

The last two defeats for the Blues had one commonality: bad striker performances. Morgan Rogers was moved there against Tottenham Hotspur but it was a largely failed experiment. Danny Welbeck got his chance against Liverpool in the cup and ghosted in a mostly mediocre display. When the lineup dropped this time, it looked worryingly like Rogers was going to play as the furthest attacker again.

articles.title: Manchester United's players, not Michael Carrick should shoulder the blame after embarrassing loss to Chelsea
articles.summary: Senior players have complained about tactics and recruitment, but a self-inflicted collapse at Chelsea showed the squad only has itself to blame
body: LONDON -- Manchester United players have been at great pains in recent weeks to point out how they have been failed by the powers that be, by those with supposedly more influence than the 11 lads on the field. On occasion, you could argue they had the measure of the situation. There's just one little note for Lisandro Martinez, Bruno Fernandes and anyone else who counts themselves among the Old Trafford mutineers.

If you're going to start demanding greater professional standards from your employers, you would be well advised to hold yourself to the same level. It would be a real problem if, for instance, you earned yourself two yellow cards in the space of 210 seconds, handing your opponents the penalty from which they win the game. Sympathy will be in quite short supply for those who complain about the head coach's tactics or the sporting director's recruitment but then, when the circumstances are right, fail to exploit prime opportunities.
